key_insight: Training vision models with a human-inspired developmental visual diet shifts them from texture- to shape-based representations, producing substantially more robust visual inference with less resource overhead.
problem_solved: Over-reliance on local texture cues makes modern vision models brittle to noise, corruptions and out-of-distribution inputs; the paper tackles how to induce more human-like, shape-based generalization without huge computational cost.
method: Design a human-inspired developmental visual diet that mimics key statistics of infant visual experience (a staged curriculum of simpler/object-centric to richer/complex scenes).
Train standard vision architectures on this developmental diet and contrast them with conventionally trained models.
Measure shifts in shape-versus-texture bias and test robustness across corruptions, perturbations and transfer tasks.
impact: Provides a practical, resource-efficient training strategy to get more human-like, shape-driven representations, improving robustness and generalization for real-world AI vision systems.

paper_title: Adopting a human developmental visual diet yields robust and shape-based AI vision
paper_authors: Zejin Lu, Sushrut Thorat, Radoslaw M. Cichy, Tim C. Kietzmann
